Source: Fundamentalists are people who will not provide personal details. For example, they may not even stand in a picture when someone wants to take a photo. About 25% of U.S. citizens fall into this category. Pragmatists are people who make decisions depending on the situation. For example, if given a bar of chocolate, they might share small personal details, but if given something more valuable, they may share more important information. Their privacy expectations change depending on the activity—like buying a product on Amazon versus doing financial transactions on ICICI. Unconcerned people are those who will even share passwords or personally identifiable information for minimal returns.
